ANNEALED ADAPTIVE SQUARE NORMAL-REFLECTED COMPARISON
2026-10-09. Internal reconstruction relative to TARGET_AND_PREMISES.txt.
All earlier freezes preserved. New sibling ANNEALED/QHC bodies UNREAD.
Source-guided analytic mechanism; no historical novelty claim.

0. WHAT CHANGES FROM FROZEN SC
The original kernels have bounded original/sign data, but ADAPTED queried
heights can be arbitrarily large. The full stationary difference is not
sup-norm bounded. Do not use SC2's bounded-pin coupling or its M^2 cluster
estimate. The projection, local force and annealed sparsity arguments below
survive; their lost constant-mode control is supplied in sections3--6.

1. EXACT ADAPTED DISINTEGRATION AND ONE STATIONARY JOINING
Condition first on one exact adjacent-sign lift of every original record.
Its uniform convex density is the ordinary hard-edge indicator times the
specified sign half-lines. An adaptive exact query transcript contributes
only decision factors measurable in already recorded values and auxiliary
randomness. Fubini, induction on the finite number of distinct queried sites
and disintegration over the stopping count therefore leave the PRODUCT
of the two conditional Gibbs kernels on unqueried coordinates. Querying
both values at the same sites produces a common fixed set in the protected
window. Freeze all original live sign coordinates internally as well;
remaining fibers have no shrinking or active individual wall constraints.

Original uniform samples almost surely have strict free-edge/sign slack;
thus their remaining fibers have positive relative free-coordinate volume,
apart from the all-pinned deterministic case. For every fiber run the two
ordinary normal-reflected baths with common variance-two Brownian increments
on common free coordinates. Outside the common graph use the appropriate
individual innovations. Compact product state space, the finite Feller
synchronous semigroup and time averaging give an invariant joining of the
two conditional uniform marginals. Time-average jointly with the static
transcript, then disintegrate for a measurable family. A null fiber needs no
probability assertion. No uniform spectral gap or runtime is invoked.

Keep this joining ONCE before force tests, tolerances or defect refinements.
Each conditional marginal is stationary and reversible in its own body.
Integrating over the ORIGINAL transcript recovers each FULL

1. AF CONDITIONAL-FIBRE VERSUS ANNEALED WORDING
Read origin CLAIMS.json AF line7 with this replacement precision:

For each almost-sure complete predictable BOTH-height query transcript,
one stationary normal-reflected joining preserves the two exact
CONDITIONAL Gibbs marginals on that transcript fibre. Averaging these
joinings over the ORIGINAL transcript law restores the FULL original
kernels, including queried coordinates, internally frozen original wall
values, all retained negative tests T and the actual sign-lift weights.
Under the target graph/buffer/anchor hypotheses, the resulting ANNEALED
energy and safe loss are <=C(1+a^2), the squared initial-fill W1p norm is
<=C_p(1+a^2), and the SAME initial fill has vanishing annealed L1 error.
For a>=1 the normalized tail/fill have threshold-uniform bounds.

The joining is chosen once BEFORE force tolerances or fill refinements.
No estimate uniform over every fixed numerical transcript is asserted.
No conditioning on future favourable events preserves this stationarity.
Main38--40 already has exactly the intended conditional/annealed scope.
This attachment resolves an abbreviated CLAIMS wording, not a new theorem.

Why literal per-transcript original full marginals are impossible:
if a queried free coordinate has a non-atomic original law, its value is
fixed in an exact-height fibre. That conditional marginal is a point mass
at the recorded value, whereas the original marginal is non-atomic.
Their equality cannot hold; only integration over the original answer
distribution restores it. No stochastic coupling choice fixes that fact.
